title: Pisces: Cryptography-based Private Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Dual-Path Retrieval
topic: Social Aspects->Privacy-preserving Statistics and Machine Learning
claim: A private system pipeline whose core novelty is a retrieval stage that protects both queries and documents across dual retrieval paths.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right, red-outlined core retrieval box, color-coded legend
description: A wide block diagram of a private RAG system, with a legend at the top left and top right. The legend maps colors to phases: preprocessing (gray), private retrieval (red outline), local data processing (light pink), private semantic retrieval (salmon), private lexical retrieval (deeper pink), private generation (blue), and encrypted information (red lock icon). At the lower left, a gray server box holds a database icon and document chunks. The chunks feed an embedding model and a tokenizer. The central red-bordered box is the core contribution. At its top, the user's local tokenizer and embedding model process the query. Below are two parallel retrieval tracks. The semantic track runs private coarse matching, then private cosine similarity, then encrypted top-K retrieval. The lexical track runs private BM25 scoring, then encrypted top-K retrieval. At the right, a blue generation box combines the retrieved chunks with the query and passes them to an LLM for secure inference. The response returns to the user. Lock icons mark encrypted data.
caption: Overview of our proposed Pisces, where the private retrieval phase is our core contribution.
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) enhances the response quality of large language models (LLMs) when handling domain-specific tasks, yet raises significant privacy concerns. This is because both the user query and documents within the knowledge base often contain sensitive or confidential information. To address these concerns, we propose $\texttt{Pisces}$, the first practical cryptography-based RAG framework that supports dual-path retrieval, while protecting both the query and documents. Along the semantic retrieval path, we reduce computation and communication overhead by leveraging a coarse-to-fine strategy. Specifically, a novel oblivious filter is used to privately select a candidate set of documents to reduce the scale of subsequent cosine similarity computations. For the lexical retrieval path, to reduce the overhead of repeatedly invoking labeled PSI, we implement a multi-instance labeled PSI protocol to compute term frequencies for BM25 scoring in a single execution. $\texttt{Pisces}$ can also be integrated with existing privacy-preserving LLM inference frameworks to achieve end-to-end privacy. Experiments demonstrate that $\texttt{Pisces}$ achieves retrieval accuracy comparable to the plaintext baselines, within a 1.87% margin.
